name: The Board
description: Two optional checks at the duty board. Neither gates the scene and neither costs anything on a failure -- the fortnight is already assigned and nothing here can change it. What these buy is information and a handle on the institution.

checks.name: Read the columns either side of your own

dc.basis: level 1 standard DC 15 -- available to anyone who thinks to look, not a specialist's roll

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The sea-wall job has been assigned twice before, to two other sections, on the two previous fortnights, and struck out both times -- and neither section logged it as completed. It was reassigned, not finished.
outcomes.success: The sea-wall job has been written up and struck out on the two previous fortnights, in two other sections' columns.
outcomes.failure: Columns of other people's tedium. Somebody has drawn a very small rude picture in the corner of the Section Four column.
outcomes.criticalFailure: As failure, and the clerk asks whether they are looking for something specific, loudly, while a queue listens.

bySkill.perception: The physical read: the same words in the same hand, struck through twice, the chalk ghost of it still there under this fortnight's paint.
bySkill.society: The administrative read: a job that moves between sections without ever being logged complete is a job somebody keeps deciding is somebody else's problem.

checks.name: Get something written in that isn't on the board

dc.basis: level 1 standard DC 15. One step easier (13) if the player actually offers her a workable swap, a named stand-in, or the correct form -- solving her problem is the intended route and should be rewarded over pure charm

outcomes.criticalSuccess: She writes it in, stamps it, and -- without being asked, and without looking up -- tells them which box on the board nobody ever actually checks.
outcomes.success: She writes it in and stamps it. It is real, it is binding for the fortnight, and it is theirs.
outcomes.failure: No. There is a queue. She is not unkind about it and the door is not closed -- come back with a swap or a form.
outcomes.criticalFailure: As failure, and she remembers the attempt the next time they come to the hatch wanting something irregular.

bySkill.diplomacy: Warmth works on her about as well as it works on a filing cabinet, but politeness plus a workable suggestion gets the suggestion actually considered.
bySkill.society: Knowing which form it goes on is most of the battle, and she visibly relaxes when somebody knows.
bySkill.deception: Inventing a plausible authorisation works, once, and she will check it afterwards. On a failure here she checks it in front of them.

notes:
NEITHER CHECK GATES ANYTHING. The fortnight is set before this scene starts and no roll here changes it. A party that rolls nothing still leaves with their bookings made and the scene's job done.

PRICING AN INVENTED APPROACH. Same ladder as the rest of Chapter One: DC 13 if it costs them something real, DC 15 for the obvious way, DC 17 if it is free or skips a step, DC 20 if it would get more than the scene was going to give. The clerk specifically rewards solving her problem over charming her -- if a player does that, drop a step.
